prompt: House passes the FY2027 NDAA 216-212. The opposition is a coalition: 204 Democrats plus 7 restraint Republicans.

fluid.text: Authorize it, and authorize it fully — a superpower that hedges on its own reach isn't being prudent, it's inviting the exact crises that cost far more than the bill in front of us.

title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027
framing: The NDAA vote on H.R. 8800 nominally asks whether to authorize defense spending, but the deeper fault line concerns what kind of military posture the funding entrenches — expansive forward power projection versus restraint and homeland/burden-sharing focus. This tension cross-cuts the party-line passage vote because both parties contain internal factions on grand strategy that don't map cleanly onto the yea/nay tally.

LF.text: A yes funds a strategy, not just a budget. Don't sign it blind — name the commitments first.

LC.text: Leadership trades objections to the NDAA for superficial provisions every year. It's time to debate the substance of the military's posture and strategy before signing another massive defense bill.

LD.text: The military's posture has been reckless for years, and it has never once had to answer for it. No on all defense spending.

RF.text: Voting no doesn't pause the deployments, only the funding. What happens in the gap?

RC.text: A vote against funding the military doesn't help the situation. Pass the NDAA and we can debate military posture and strategy later.

RD.text: Our military is engaged in multiple dynamic conflicts. Now isn't the time to debate strategy with woke leftists.
